reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a PUBG Mobile hack or guide promising free UC and Battle Points through a generator page that asks for a username and device. It then instructs viewers to download and open two apps, with the Castle Clash App Store page appearing after that instruction as part of the participation flow. The frames do not establish that the resources were delivered or that any account change or loss occurred.

citations.quote: PUBG Mobile Hack - Free UC and Battle Points on Android/iOS
What this video can tech me is how to get unlimited free UC and Battle points.

opening.argument: The material presents an instructional claim, not proof of a completed scam. The description says the video can teach viewers how to obtain the resources, but it does not document a completed delivery, an account change, a payment, or a loss. The supplied gameplay and inventory frames likewise show the game being used, not a confirmed transaction or harm. A careful viewer could therefore treat the claim as something to investigate rather than as established deception.

citations.quote: What this video can tech me is how to get unlimited free UC and Battle points.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The title and description use promotional language, but neither proves that the presenter obtained money, credentials, or any other benefit from viewers. The generator sequence and the app-store screen show a procedure, while the prosecution concedes that delivery and account impact are unestablished. That unresolved outcome is consistent with an unverified tutorial claim, not enough by itself to establish a scam.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of proven loss does not make the solicitation benign. The title explicitly calls it a hack for free resources, and the description says the resources will be on the viewer's account for many decades. The visible flow asks for a username and device and then directs viewers to download apps, which is actionable participation rather than a neutral warning or test.

citations.quote: PUBG Mobile Hack - Free UC and Battle Points on Android/iOS
will be on your PUBG account for many decades

opening.argument: This is most naturally read as an operational walkthrough of a mobile-game process. The description repeatedly characterizes the content as a guide, and the frames show a sequence: a PUBG screen, a browser page requesting a username and device, a generator progress screen, an app-store listing, and subsequent gameplay. Showing those screens is consistent with demonstrating what a viewer would encounter. The record does not establish that the creator personally solicited payment, obtained credentials, or falsely confirmed a successful result.

citations.quote: Look at all the steps from guide

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the sequence a guide does not answer what the guide directs viewers to do. The browser page is labeled as a generator, and the overlay instructs viewers to download and open two apps. Those are the operative steps, not merely commentary about a third-party scam. The later game footage does not convert that conduct into neutral education.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The format is instructional, but the instruction teaches viewers to pursue purported free game assets through an external generator and app downloads. The description calls the method a hack and cheats, while the frames show a username/device prompt and a multi-app requirement. Demonstration framing therefore describes how the promotion is delivered; it does not remove its deceptive reward claim.

citations.quote: PUBG Mobile Hack - Free UC and Battle Points on Android/iOS

opening.argument: At most, this is a promotion for a purported game-reward service or referral flow. The promised subject is ordinary in-game currency and battle points, and the visible path reaches an App Store listing for another game before returning to gameplay. Crucially, the supplied evidence does not show a deposit, paid purchase, password request, guaranteed financial return, downline income, or confirmed account compromise. Even the username-and-device screen does not establish that sensitive credentials were collected. Those missing mechanisms support treating this as an ordinary rewards promotion rather than a demonstrated scam.

citations.quote: unlimited free UC and Battle points

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution does not need to show a monetary deposit to prove this type of deception. Its own account identifies a purported generator, a username/device prompt, and app downloads as the participation flow. An App Store page and later gameplay show only that applications were displayed or used; they do not establish that the flow was legitimate, but they also do not supply the missing proof of a scam.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A scam need not demand money or a password when it induces users to follow a false reward process and download unrelated apps. The description promises that free resources will be placed on the account and invokes the method as already tested by top gamers. The username/device prompt and two-app instruction are concrete participation requirements, while no frame confirms that PUBG rewards were ever delivered.
